answer: Registration binds each identity to one ferrous plate of key-set mass, two kilograms, one face polished to a mirror. A jade stylus of standard hardness drawn once across that face cuts grooves whose depth follows the alloy; auditors record its mass, magnetic moment, and groove map. Each epoch it is weighed, assayed, and re-imaged; any mismatch ends its weight. A farm with 1,000 identities casts two tonnes into 1,000 plates and keeps each presentable; one honest agent casts one plate once. Split between two names, a plate's mass halves below its registered value, and the assay rejects both.
